content:
FRP gratings needs little maintenance, but the little it needs is regular: inspect twice a year, clean with mild detergent and water, check fasteners, and reseal any damage promptly. This routine extends FRP service life to 20-30 years and prevents small issues from becoming structural problems.

Unlike steel, FRP does not rust; unlike wood, it does not rot. As a fibre-reinforced plastic, its longevity is governed by the resin matrix and surface protection rather than by corrosion. Its maintenance load is low but real: a six-monthly inspection, periodic cleaning to remove dirt and chemical residue, fastener checks, and prompt repair of any surface damage. The two things that actually shorten FRP life are neglected damage (moisture ingress at cut edges) and aggressive environments (UV, chemicals) on unprotected surfaces. Address both with a simple routine and FRP products routinely deliver 20+ year service lives.


#### A Simple Maintenance Plan
| Monthly (heavy use)| Visual check, remove debris |
| --- | --- |
|Every 6 months | Inspection + cleaning + fastener check |
| Annually | Full inspection, edge-seal check, UV coating review |
| After events | Post-damage, chemical spill, or overload check |

Adapt the frequency to the environment — a chemical plant needs more frequent attention than an indoor mezzanine. ASTM weathering standards provide the testing framework that predicts how outdoor FRP ages. Keep a simple log: date, findings, actions. Consistency beats intensity.


## Regular Inspection Points

- Surface: chalking, cracks, delamination, fiber bloom.
- Edges: sealed? moisture staining? fiber exposure?
